annotations.title: Point-in-time fundamentals: what was filed as of a date, before restatement

description: Call this when the question is about what was known on a past date (a backtest, an audit, "what did the 10-K say at the time"), not about the current restated figures. Returns, for each fiscal period filed on or before `date`, the value as it stood on that date (the original filing, or a later filing for the same period if it came before `date`), the filing date, the XBRL tag, a sec.gov link, and `restated_after_date` when a later filing changed it. Values are as printed, not split-adjusted. Inputs: `ticker` (path), `date` (YYYY-MM-DD, required), `metrics` (comma-separated snake_case names, default revenues,net_income,eps_diluted,operating_cash_flow,free_cash_flow,stockholders_equity,total_debt,shares_outstanding), `period` (annual|quarterly), `limit` (periods, default 4). Example: GET /as-filed/AAPL?date=2020-02-01&metrics=revenues,net_income. If the company had filed none of it by `date`, the answer has no periods, the flag `nothing_filed_by_date` and `earliest_filed` (the first filing date on record). A 503 `as-filed-unavailable` means there is no as-filed history for the company to answer from; it is not charged, and GET /fundamentals has the current figures. 0.01 credits. (GET https://app.deepvalues.ai/api/v1/as-filed/{ticker} — 0.01 credits per call; works with no credentials up to 5 call(s)/day per address)

date.description: The day to look back from (YYYY-MM-DD, 2009-01-01 or later, not in the future).

limit.description: How many of the most recent periods filed by `date` to return.
